ref.title: Acute effects of brief exercise on alcohol craving among young adults with problematic alcohol use: A systematic review

sources.title: Acute Effects of Brief Exercise on Alcohol Craving Among Young Adults With Problematic Alcohol Use: A Systematic Review
money: This study was funded by the Spanish Ministry of Health (Government Delegation for the National Plan on Drugs, code 2024I030 to R.D.M.‐F.) and FEDER/Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation and the National Research Agency (AEI) (MCIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033/FEDER, UE, code PID2022‐137601OA‐I00 to P.S.‐P).

design.quote: This systematic review examined the effects of brief exercise interventions on alcohol craving in young adults with problematic alcohol use or alcohol use disorder (AUD) and explored available evidence on associated neurobiological responses.
design.text: A systematic review of studies on brief exercise interventions for alcohol craving in young adults with problematic alcohol use or alcohol use disorder.

findings.where: Discussion › Neurobiological Processes Associated With Alcohol Use and Acute Exercise
findings.quote: At the neurochemical level, alcohol has been linked to persistent adaptations in mesolimbic dopaminergic circuits involved in incentive salience and craving
findings.text: Alcohol is linked to persistent adaptations in mesolimbic dopaminergic circuits that are involved in incentive salience and craving.

findings.where: Discussion › Neurobiological Processes Associated With Alcohol Use and Acute Exercise
findings.quote: In addition, NMDA receptor‐mediated glutamatergic transmission contributes to synaptic adaptations underlying dependence and relapse vulnerability.
findings.text: NMDA receptor-mediated glutamatergic transmission contributes to synaptic adaptations that underlie dependence and relapse vulnerability.

findings.where: Discussion › Neurobiological Processes Associated With Alcohol Use and Acute Exercise
findings.quote: alcohol‐related cues elicit robust dopaminergic responses in the ventral striatum and associated limbic structures, which may be related to compulsive consumption patterns
findings.text: Alcohol-related cues cause robust dopaminergic responses in the ventral striatum and associated limbic structures, which may be related to compulsive consumption patterns.

limits.quote: Future research should therefore prioritize adequately powered studies using standardised craving and neurobiological measures, as well as designs that allow for the assessment of temporal dynamics and real‐world relevance of exercise‐induced effects on alcohol craving.
limits.text: Future research needs to use standardized measures and designs that assess the temporal dynamics and real-world relevance of exercise effects on alcohol craving.
